SC-2025-H3305.s: The act makes extra budget funding for South Carolina for fiscal year 2026-2027. It affects state spending for that year. It was signed by the governor and took effect on September 1, 2026.
SC-2025-H3305.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5060.s: This act changes the St. John’s Fire District by adding more members to its commission and updating its buying rules. It also repeals a 1978 law section about adding one more member. It became effective on May 19, 2026.
SC-2025-H5060.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5126.s: The act sets the state budget for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026. It provides money for ordinary state government costs, controls how those funds are spent, and covers how state government will operate during that year and other related matters. It became Act No. 259, and some items were vetoed by the governor.
SC-2025-H5126.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5127.s: This joint resolution would set aside money from South Carolina’s Capital Reserve Fund for fiscal year 2025-2026. It would also let any unused money carry over into later fiscal years and be spent for the same purposes. It became law in 2026.
SC-2025-H5127.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5261.s: This joint resolution would extend the deadline to get alcohol server training to May 1, 2026. It affects people who must complete that training under state law. It became law on March 9, 2026.
SC-2025-H5261.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5537.s: The resolution would direct the state to transfer the National Guard armory in Dillon County to the City of Dillon, the armory in Timmonsville to the City of Timmonsville, and the armory in Barnwell to Barnwell County. It affects those local governments and the state agency handling the transfer. It became effective on May 19, 2026.
SC-2025-H5537.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5641.s: The act repeals the law that created the Florence Memorial Stadium Commission. It affects the commission created under the 1948 act. It became law on May 19, 2026.
SC-2025-H5641.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5653.s: The act changes how people file to run for the Lee County school board, how board elections are run, and how empty seats on the board are filled. It also sets yearly pay for board members. It became effective on May 19, 2026.
SC-2025-H5653.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5747.s: A House resolution congratulates Ford Wilder, a recent Wilson Hall graduate, on signing to play basketball for the University of South Carolina. It also wishes him success in his school and sports career, and the resolution was adopted.
SC-2025-H5747.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5748.s: The resolution would give the South Carolina House chamber to the Religious Liberty Conference on Wednesday, January 6, 2027. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5748.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5751.s: A House resolution would recognize and honor Vanester Evans for her faithful and devoted service to Saint Paul African Methodist Episcopal Church in Horry County. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5751.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5760.s: The resolution congratulates Rhiannon Wyatt of Pauline-Glenn Springs Elementary School for being named the 2026 Spartanburg County School District 6 Teacher of the Year. It also expresses appreciation for her service to children and wishes her success in the future. The House adopted it on August 11, 2026.
SC-2025-H5760.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5763.s: The House adopted a resolution expressing sorrow over the death of Eartha "Nell" Fuller of Orangeburg County and extending sympathy to her family and friends. It is a formal statement from the House, not a change to state law.
SC-2025-H5763.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5764.s: The House resolution would express sorrow over the death of Franklin Gregory "Goree" Smith of Calhoun County and extend sympathy to his family and friends. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5764.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5766.s: The House resolution congratulates Hattie Mae Green of Orangeburg County on her 103rd birthday and wishes her continued health and happiness. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5766.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5767.s: The resolution celebrates the 150th anniversary of St. Paul African Methodist Episcopal Church. It also congratulates and honors Reverend Andrew J. Jordan and the church congregation for their years of service to the Creston community. The measure was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5767.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5770.s: The resolution would recognize and honor the members of the Greenville Girl Friends at their 25th anniversary celebration. It would also extend best wishes for many more years of friendship, service, and conviviality.
SC-2025-H5770.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5773.s: A House resolution that congratulates Reese Stoney, Miss Clarendon, and commends her discipline, goals, and talent. It was introduced and adopted in the South Carolina House.
SC-2025-H5773.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5774.s: Lawmakers adopted a resolution to recognize the Pendleton Recreation Association 12U All-Star baseball team for its 2026 season. It also congratulates the team for winning the South Carolina D2 "0" Zone state championship and reaching the World Series in Mississippi.
SC-2025-H5774.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5777.s: The resolution honors and recognizes Aristidis "Harry" Anagnostaras-Adams for his work in global mining and finance. It was introduced and adopted in the South Carolina House.
SC-2025-H5777.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5778.s: A House resolution congratulates Henry F. Saamoi, the executive governor of Liberia’s central bank, for his leadership, public service, and work to modernize Liberia’s financial system. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5778.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5782.s: The resolution honors the life and achievements of Mr. Abdoul Karim Diallo, who was the director general of Sonoco Group. It was introduced and adopted by the South Carolina House.
SC-2025-H5782.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5784.s: The House adopted a resolution to congratulate Henri-Claude Oyima, chairman and group chief executive officer of BGFIBANK Group. It recognizes his leadership and his work in African banking, regional capital markets, and private sector growth.
SC-2025-H5784.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5786.s: A House resolution honors the life and achievements of His Excellency Mai Mala Buni, the executive governor of Yobe State, Nigeria. It is a formal statement by lawmakers about an African political and administrative leader. The resolution was introduced and adopted on August 11, 2026.
SC-2025-H5786.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5787.s: The House adopted a resolution to recognize His Excellency Hope Uzodimma, the executive governor of Imo State in Nigeria. It is a formal statement of recognition by lawmakers.
SC-2025-H5787.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5788.s: The House adopted a resolution to recognize and honor Alhaji Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, who serves as a special adviser to the president of Nigeria.
SC-2025-H5788.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5790.s: A concurrent resolution asks the state transportation department to name a part of U.S. Highway 21 in York County the "Sheriff J. Elbert Pope Memorial Highway." It would also ask for signs or markers to be put along that stretch of road.
SC-2025-H5790.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5792.s: Lawmakers adopted a resolution expressing sorrow over the death of Charles Ernest "Chuck" Black Jr. of Marlboro County. It also extends sympathy to his family and friends.
SC-2025-H5792.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5795.s: The House adopted a resolution to express sorrow over the death of Katherine Liles, celebrate her life, and extend sympathy to her family and friends. The resolution honors her as a native of Moncks Corner.
SC-2025-H5795.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5796.s: The House passed a resolution expressing deep sorrow over Joseph McCants's death and sympathy for his family and friends. It is a formal statement by lawmakers and does not change state law.
SC-2025-H5796.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5798.s: A House resolution would honor and congratulate Mark A. Williams of Sumter County for receiving the inaugural Swan Lake Sentinel Award at the 2026 Swan Lake Premiere Film Festival. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5798.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5799.s: A House resolution that expresses sorrow over the death of Harold Raymond Waynick Jr. of Sumter County and extends sympathy to his family and friends.
SC-2025-H5799.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5800.s: This resolution celebrates the 160th anniversary of Friendship United Methodist Church. It also congratulates and commends Reverend Dr. Ernest W. Frierson and the congregation for their years of service to the Nesmith community. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5800.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5802.s: A House resolution would recognize Irmo Insurance Agency on its 50th anniversary of service in South Carolina. It would also congratulate the company on 50 years of business in the state.
SC-2025-H5802.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5803.s: The resolution would recognize and honor Usher Raymond and Chris Brown for their music careers. It would also welcome them to Columbia and South Carolina for their performance at Williams-Brice Stadium.
SC-2025-H5803.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5804.s: A House resolution would congratulate Nixon Woods Wooten and offer best wishes to Sopharvathdy Vandy Vorn on their upcoming wedding. It was introduced and adopted in the South Carolina House.
SC-2025-H5804.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5805.s: A House resolution recognizes and congratulates First Baptist Church of Blacksburg on its 150th anniversary. It also commends the church for 150 years of service to God and the community.
SC-2025-H5805.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5806.s: This resolution was adopted and recognizes August 30, 2026, as "Sammie D. Simmons Day" in South Carolina. It celebrates Pastor Sammie D. Simmons on his birthday and honors his leadership and service.
SC-2025-H5806.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5807.s: A House resolution expresses sorrow over the death of Alica Van Rensalier Lewis James of Orangeburg and extends sympathy to her family and friends. It was introduced and adopted by the House.
SC-2025-H5807.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5808.s: A House resolution would honor Captain Gregory R. "Reed" Koepp II of the U.S. Navy on his retirement after 27 years of service. It would also recognize his leadership at Joint Base Lindsey Graham, formerly Joint Base Charleston, and his work connecting the military and civilian communities in the South Carolina Lowcountry. The resolution was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-H5808.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5809.s: The resolution recognizes and honors the Clinton High School baseball team, coaches, and school officials for an outstanding 2026 season. It also congratulates them for winning the Class AA state baseball championship title.
SC-2025-H5809.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5810.s: The resolution recognizes the City of Georgetown, South Carolina, as a designated site in a UNESCO project about enslaved peoples, resistance, liberty, and heritage. It was introduced and adopted in the House.
SC-2025-H5810.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5811.s: This resolution says the South Carolina House supports hunting deer with dogs when done lawfully and responsibly. It also says private property owners’ rights should be respected, and that major changes to the rules for hunting deer with dogs on private land should be made by the General Assembly. It calls on the Natural Resources Board to follow the policy choices made by lawmakers.
SC-2025-H5811.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-H5813.s: The bill would create the South Carolina Community Investment Fund. It would set rules for when money in the fund could be spent, use a per-district formula to divide funds, and add rules for how the fund is run, tracked, and reported. It would affect how state money is allocated to districts.
SC-2025-H5813.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1011.s: This joint resolution would direct a state agency to transfer the National Guard armory in Barnwell, South Carolina, to Barnwell County. It was signed by the governor on May 19, 2026, and took effect on that date.
SC-2025-S1011.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1018.s: The bill would change the rules for South Carolina scholarship programs. It would add the Classic Learning Test, or CLT, as an allowed test for the Palmetto Fellows Scholarship, and it would also let ACT and CLT scores count for the LIFE Scholarship and for a state education rule on qualified residents. The changes would affect students applying for these scholarships.
SC-2025-S1018.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1062.s: Approved state higher education rules on how tuition and fees are set. It affects the State Commission on Higher Education and schools covered by those rules. The measure was signed by the governor and took effect on May 18, 2026.
SC-2025-S1062.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1162.s: The law changes how trustees for Anderson County School District 2 are chosen. It says six of the seven board members must be elected from single-member districts, meaning each one is elected from a separate area. It took effect on May 18, 2026.
SC-2025-S1162.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1218.s: A Senate resolution would recognize and honor Brian Rudick for his many years of service and leadership as a Scouting America Scoutmaster. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-S1218.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1219.s: A Senate resolution would congratulate the Southside High School boys soccer team, coaches, and school officials for an outstanding season. It also honors them for winning the South Carolina Class AAAA boys soccer state championship, and it was adopted.
SC-2025-S1219.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1221.s: This concurrent resolution recognizes and honors Major James Capers Jr. for his service in the U.S. Marine Corps and his heroism. It also congratulates him on receiving the Medal of Honor for his actions in Vietnam.
SC-2025-S1221.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1228.s: A Senate resolution would recognize September 8-11, 2026, as "Marion County Liberty Week" in South Carolina. It would also commemorate Marion County's role in the American Revolutionary War.
SC-2025-S1228.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1229.s: A Senate resolution recognizes August 13, 2026, as "Mrs. Felicia Douglas Littlejohn Day" in South Carolina. It also commends Mrs. Littlejohn for her 25-year career supporting financial literacy, economic empowerment, civic leadership, and the Greenville community. The resolution was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-S1229.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1230.s: A Senate resolution to congratulate Frank Hatten on his retirement and wish him well in the years ahead.
SC-2025-S1230.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1236.s: The Senate adopted a resolution to congratulate Dr. Byron L. Battle Sr. on his fifth anniversary as pastor of Tabernacle Baptist Church. It also commends him for his many years of service to his congregation and the Greenville community.
SC-2025-S1236.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1237.s: A Senate resolution would congratulate HCS Scholars Academy High School for winning the 2026 Class 1A FAFSA First Challenge. It would also commend the school for its many years of service to the people of South Carolina.
SC-2025-S1237.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1240.s: The Senate adopted a resolution to recognize and honor the Boykin Spaniel Society for its work to preserve and promote the Boykin Spaniel breed. It is a formal statement of thanks, not a law that changes state rules.
SC-2025-S1240.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S1241.s: The Senate would express sorrow at the death of Chief Deputy Clifton J. Howle and extend sympathy to his family and friends. It was introduced and adopted.
SC-2025-S1241.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S136.s: The law requires the state to dismiss and expunge certain pending unlawful handgun possession charges that happened before the South Carolina Constitutional Carry/Second Amendment Preservation Act of 2024. It affects people with those pending gun possession cases. The dismissal of those charges cannot be used as a reason for civil lawsuits tied to the arrest.
SC-2025-S136.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S623.s: The act exempts Georgetown County from some building rules and lets the county use AE standards in its flood damage prevention ordinance instead. AE standards are rules used for building in flood-prone areas. It became effective on February 10, 2026.
SC-2025-S623.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)

SC-2025-S769.s: This joint resolution would keep state government funded if the 2026-2027 budget is not in place when that fiscal year starts. It would also set out some exceptions. It became law on May 15, 2026.
SC-2025-S769.src: South Carolina legislature, description (via Open States)
